creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 13, item 1.

```rad
a = ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]
b = a[:2] + ["X", "Y"]
print(a)   // [ "a", "b", "X", "Y", "e" ]
```

Reproduces on main. In the real script, `lines = lines[:start] + block + lines[end:]` dropped a line, because `lines[:start] + block` overwrote `lines` before `lines[end:]` was read. Nothing errors and the expression reads as pure.

A list slice shares the original's backing array, and `+` appends into the spare capacity. Copy on slice (or clip the slice's capacity) and add a regression test that `a[:n] + x` leaves `a` intact.

Where: `core/interpreter.go:1383` `sliced.Values = coerced.Values[start:end]`.
title: a[:n] + list overwrites the original list a
